topic: The Mystery of Being Both: Superposition and Quantum States
target_audience: Introductory University Students or Advanced High School Students

sections.title: The Classical vs. Quantum Divide
lecture_lines: Classical systems exist in one definite state at once.
A light switch is either strictly ON or OFF.
Quantum systems are different; they don't choose sides yet.
Imagine a spinning coin, being both heads and tails.
This "bothness" is the core of the quantum world.

Display text "Quantum: Both?" (#00FFFF) and show a coin spinning.
Show the coin blurred to represent multiple states.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Vector Map
lecture_lines: We can map quantum possibilities using 2D geometry.
Outcomes are represented as axes on a graph.
A quantum state is an arrow within this space.
animations: Draw 2D axes: Y is "|Heads⟩" (#FFFF00), X is "|Tails⟩" (#00FFFF).
Draw a white vector pointing straight up on the Y-axis.
Draw a white vector pointing right on the X-axis.

sections.title: Defining the Quantum State (|ψ⟩)
lecture_lines: We call this quantum state vector 'Ket Psi'.
It can point anywhere between our two outcome axes.
Crucially, the length of this arrow is always one.
animations: Display "|ψ⟩" (#FF69B4) and a unit circle on a 2D plane.
Draw a vector "|ψ⟩" (#FF69B4) starting at origin, ending on the circle.
Rotate the vector "|ψ⟩" smoothly around the origin, keeping its length constant.

sections.title: The Math of Superposition
lecture_lines: Mathematical superposition combines these states using Greek letters.
Alpha and Beta represent the vector's horizontal and vertical shadows.
These 'amplitudes' define the probability of each outcome.
The squared sum of these shadows must equal one.
This ensures the total probability always remains one hundred percent.
animations: Display the superposition equation: "|ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩" (#FFFFFF).
Show a vector at a 45-degree angle on the coordinate plane.
Draw projections (dotted lines) from the vector tip to both axes.
Label projections α (#00FF00) on X-axis and β (#FF0000) on Y-axis.
Display and highlight "α² + β² = 1" (#FFFFFF) next to the vector.

sections.title: The Collapse: The Act of Measuring
lecture_lines: Measuring a system forces it to pick one state.
The vector instantly snaps to a single classical axis.
This sudden change is known as 'Wavefunction Collapse'.
Probability depends on the square of the state's amplitude.
The mystery of 'both' vanishes upon our observation.
animations: Start with the 45-degree vector and labels α, β.

The vector snaps to the Y-axis |0⟩ (#FFFF00) instantly.
Fade out the original diagonal vector and the α projection.

sections.title: Application: Quantum Computing
lecture_lines: Classical bits process one path at a time.
Qubits explore every possible path simultaneously.
This allows computers to solve complex problems instantly.
animations: Show a maze [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/maze.svg] with one white dot moving through a path.
Show the same maze [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/maze.svg] filled with many blue dots (#00FFFF) spreading out.
